content.comment_body: I am using [product_name] with a load cell and an A/D amplifier. After calibrating and testing, the analog reading never shows zero, but instead displays values like 0.05 or 0.1. When checking with a multi-meter, the voltage was about 1 mV. Is there a way to make [product_name] ignore such small voltages?
No, this voltage is simply too low. You should look for an amplifier module designed for load cells that outputs either 0-10V or 0/4-20mA.
I am already using an amplifier and it functions properly, but when the scale is empty, it still provides these small readings. I would like it to show only 0.00 when nothing is on the scale.

If I understand correctly, you want to adjust the display since the load cell has a small error at zero. With an analog multiplexer, you can connect up to four different values using two control inputs.
You can refine your analog signal by applying a mathematical operation to adjust it slightly higher or lower.
The analog multiplexer works effectively. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: A user faced an issue where their [product_name], combined with a load cell and amplifier, consistently showed a small nonzero analog reading even with no load present. This was attributed to small voltage fluctuations or zero point errors from the hardware setup. Community members suggested both hardware and software methods to ignore or correct these minimal signals and achieve a true zero display.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for the [product_name] system to reliably display zero when the load cell is unloaded, disregarding insignificant voltage changes. They seek an easy solution, either through hardware setup or software configuration, to offset or filter out such small signals.
